headline: Headmistress stabbed 27 times to death for money, two students arrested in India
summary: Police in Nalgonda, India, have uncovered the brutal murder of a 48-year-old school headmistress, Kallu Roopa Reddy, by two of her own 10th-grade students, motivated by greed for money and a lavish lifestyle.
details: Police in Nalgonda, Telangana, India, have arrested two 10th-grade students for the brutal murder of their school's headmistress, Kallu Roopa Reddy (48). The students confessed to stabbing her 27 times to death, motivated by a desire for money and a lavish lifestyle.

Roopa Reddy was the headmistress and director of Nagarjuna Public School in Kondamallepalli. Her mutilated body was found at her home on August 12, with the autopsy confirming 27 stab wounds. Her husband was in Hyderabad at the time of the incident.

Five Nalgonda police teams investigated, questioning over 80 people and reviewing CCTV footage. A critical clue emerged when the victim, speaking to a relative just before her phone went dead, uttered the word 'Babu'.
This led police to monitor students, discovering that five 10th-grade students were absent on the day of the murder. Two of them were subsequently found to be spending lavishly and partying.

The two students were detained and confessed, revealing they had planned the murder for five days. They entered her home wearing gloves and monkey caps to steal 2.5 lakh rupees. When their caps came off, revealing their identities, they stabbed her repeatedly.

After the murder, they buried their blood-stained clothes and went on a pleasure trip to Goa. Police recovered 1.54 lakh rupees, the victim's mobile phone, and an iPhone bought with the stolen money from the accused.
Further investigation revealed that before the incident, the students had searched video streaming sites for 'how to get rich quickly'.
caption:

headline_marked: [[Coke Studio Bangla releases new song 'Mulluk']] featuring tea garden artists' stories of identity
headline: Coke Studio Bangla releases new song 'Mulluk' featuring tea garden artists' stories of identity
summary: The song, "Mulluk," is the fourth track of the fourth season and tells the story of tea garden artists' history, their desire to return to their roots, and their search for identity and home. It draws inspiration from the 'Mulluk Cholo Andolon' movement.
details: "Mulluk," a folk song passed down through generations by tea garden artists, has been re-arranged and released by Coke Studio Bangla. It is the fourth song of their fourth season, released last night.

The song explores the history of tea garden artists, their longing to return to their roots, and their search for identity and home. Its concept is drawn from the 'Mulluk Cholo Andolon' movement and the struggles of tea artists from a century ago.

Shibu Kumar Shil added new lyrics to parts of the folk song and composed the tune. Tea artists Ronju Tanti and Ronjit Tanti lent their voices, accompanied by music from Meghdol and the rhythmic beats of Sreemangal's Dhol.

Coke Studio Bangla stated in a press release that the song is dedicated to all those who work hard and dream of a better future. The track is available on Coke Studio Bangla's official channel and various digital streaming platforms.
